You're looking at the numbers, but I need to remind you of the pattern you've been tracking in your Notion log since January. You've been reviewing Zillow estimates for your current home at 47 Elmwood Terrace, noting the 'quick-sale' range is realistically $275K-$280K, while the current listing is around $310K. You've also been calculating your monthly cushion: roughly $3,700 in (contract + dividends) minus $3,400 in spending, leaving about $300 slack before the makerspace earmark comes off the top. 

You've been debating this for months. You mentioned in your logs that you 'act broke when you're not broke' and have a specific fear reflex about spending money on yourself, even when it's objectively available. You've been delaying purchases like the Coursera course ($340) and the LED panel ($280) because they feel like the kind of thing you should wait for the grant resubmission to be done. 

If you move, you're not just moving a house; you're moving into a new financial rhythm. You've been tracking your assets (Vanguard ~$185K, Ally ~$14K, Roth ~$90K, TIAA ~$240K) and your income stability (Jenna Park contract, contract work). But you've also been noting the 'fear reflex' that makes you avoid spending on yourself. 

I'd recommend running the numbers for the new place against your current 'quick-sale' estimate. If the new place is in a similar price bracket, you might find the math works out, but the psychological cost of the move might be higher than the financial gain. You've been saying you don't want to be 'chemically checked out' for flights, preferring to be uncomfortable and present. That same energy might apply here. 

Also, you've been tracking your health closely (blood work, back issues, heart rate). Moving is a stressor. You've been doing the breathing exercises and box breathing. You might want to factor in the recovery time for your body and mind, not just the financials. 

You've been saying you don't want to be your father on this one either. Your father would have taken the money and regretted it. You've been saying you're not him. But you've also been saying you're 'mediocre' and that you need to build something instead. 

What's the specific move you're considering? And what's the 'why' behind it? Is it the money? The space? The feeling of being somewhere else? You've been saying you need to feel like you're 'actually doing the right thing' when you're doing math, art, and teaching all at once. Does moving fit that triad?
